terra.problem: Papa says he has blurry edges, but his edges were made sharp when he was renewed.
The people give a collective reply. The text does not say that nobody stepped up with a complaint.
The text does not say that nobody raised a hand or that the room was quiet.
Joshua's role as a leader and Moses' helper is outside this passage and needs a reference.
The text does not give Samuel's reason for telling them this. Marking his intention as a guess does not establish it.
The trouble is described in verse 9, not the next verse. Verse 10 tells of the fathers crying out and confessing.
Dwelling securely does not establish that all their fear was over.
The oven comparison makes the LORD's role as King part of the joke.
Calling Samuel a prophet is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
Kish's relationship to Saul is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The joke turns the LORD's hand into a humorous image of Him hugging the people.
The text does not say the people stood still. It does not permit inventing an action, even as a guess.
The text says the people feared; it does not say nobody cheered.
The text does not say that nobody doubted after the thunder and rain.
The burnt-batch line extends the promise about the LORD's people to anyone who has made a mistake, which the passage does not say.
Saying Samuel judged for years uses a fact from outside this passage without a reference.
This is the last passage in the story group, but the explanation says the story is not over and teases more to come.
